claims.text: The starting Nb-Ta-dominated superconducting HEA is a disordered BCC or related solid solution.
Increasing Ti and adding Hf or Zr will enhance local compositional disorder.
Higher Ti content will increase lattice distortion.
The Ti-induced disorder and lattice distortion will alter the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The Ti-induced disorder and lattice distortion will alter electron-phonon coupling strength.
Modulation of superconducting pairing interactions by compositional disorder can increase Tc.
A Ti-rich modification will have a higher Tc than the Nb-Ta-dominated baseline.
A Ti-rich modification may have a higher upper critical field than the Nb-Ta-dominated baseline.
Conventional type-A Nb-Ta-rich superconducting HEAs typically have Tc values in the 4-9 K range.
The highest upper critical field reported for conventional type-A HEA superconductors is close to 12 T.
Most widely studied type-A HEA superconductors contain substantial Nb and Ta and typically less than 20 at.% Ti.
Titanium-rich ternary Nb-Ti-Hf and Nb-Ti-Ta and quaternary Nb-Ti-Ta-Hf alloys have shown the highest upper critical fields within their respective reported series.
Using identical mechanical-milling and sintering conditions will ensure homogeneous single-phase baseline and modified microstructures.
The magnitude of any Tc or upper-critical-field enhancement is uncertain because Ti-rich HEAs have limited prior characterization.
The superconducting response may be sensitive to synthesis conditions.
Formation of intermetallic phases would disrupt superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The upper-critical-field increase is described only as possible, but the falsification rule uses failure to increase either Tc or μ0Hc2 as a reason for falsification. Thus, unchanged μ0Hc2 could formally falsify an effect that was not required by the prediction.

The boundary excludes alloys that develop significant intermetallic phases, whereas the falsification rule treats formation of such phases as falsifying the hypothesis. That outcome instead places the sample outside the stated applicability domain.
